headline: CF strength and new launches outrun opex, guidance raised
summary_short: Vertex reported Q2 2026 total revenue of $3,333.9M (+12.5% y/y) and GAAP net income of $1,099.8M (+6.5% y/y, $4.31 diluted EPS), and raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $13.1-13.2 billion from $12.95-13.1 billion previously.
summary_long: CF therapies remained the core growth engine — ALYFTREK uptake and higher CF net pricing lifted U.S. revenue 11% y/y, while ex-US revenue rose 14% aided by favorable FX — with diversification revenue from CASGEVY (+151% y/y to $76.4M) and JOURNAVX (quadrupling to $49.6M) layering on top. Combined R&D/AIPR&D/SG&A spend rose on JOURNAVX commercialization and renal-franchise (povetacicept) investment, but revenue growth outpaced it, lifting GAAP operating income 8.0% y/y. Vertex raised FY2026 revenue guidance to $13.1-13.2B (from $12.95-13.1B) while reiterating its opex and tax-rate ranges; guidance excludes the pending ~$10.0B Crinetics Pharmaceuticals acquisition, expected to close Q3 2026. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities rose to $13.6B from $12.3B at 2025 year-end.

drivers.explanation: CEO Kewalramani framed the quarter as expanding CF leadership while diversifying into sickle cell disease, beta thalassemia, acute pain, and — via the pending Crinetics acquisition — rare endocrine disease as a fifth pillar.

U.S. growth (+11% y/y) came from CF patient demand including new ALYFTREK initiations, higher CF net pricing, and CASGEVY/JOURNAVX contributions; ex-US growth (+14%) added ALYFTREK uptake, more CASGEVY infusions, and a favorable FX impact.
Cost of sales rose 20% y/y off a small base ($407.5M to $489.2M), but the larger $369M revenue increase outpaced the $82M cost increase in dollar terms, expanding gross profit.

Revenue growth outpaced a rise in combined R&D/AIPR&D/SG&A expenses, which increased on commercial investment behind the JOURNAVX acute-pain launch and the renal franchise build-out led by povetacicept.
